safety.overview: Safety is the foundation of all climbing, rigging, and cutting. Professional arborists follow strict safety rules to prevent injury, avoid accidents, and manage risk in dangerous environments.

ppe.helmet: Arborist-rated helmet with chin strap. Protects from falling limbs and impacts.
ppe.gloves: Protect hands from rope burn, cuts, and abrasion.
ppe.eyeProtection: Safety glasses or mesh visor to block chips and debris.
ppe.hearingProtection: Ear muffs or plugs to reduce chainsaw noise.
ppe.chaps: Chainsaw chaps prevent leg injuries during ground cutting.
ppe.boots: Steel-toe or climbing boots with strong grip.

climbingSafety.twoPoint: Always maintain two points of attachment when cutting.
climbingSafety.anchorSelection: Choose strong, healthy limbs for anchors.
climbingSafety.ropeInspection: Inspect rope for glazing, cuts, or core shots.
climbingSafety.gearCheck: Check harness, carabiners, lanyards, and ascenders before climbing.
climbingSafety.communication: Use clear signals with ground crew.

riggingSafety.loadControl: Understand load weight, rope angles, and friction.
riggingSafety.anchorStrength: Rig only from strong limbs or trunks.
riggingSafety.frictionDevices: Use devices to control speed and prevent shock-loading.
riggingSafety.dropZone: Clear drop zone and keep people out of danger.

cuttingSafety.sawHandling: Keep two hands on saw, avoid kickback zone, and maintain stable stance.
cuttingSafety.cutPlanning: Plan cuts before making them. Identify compression and tension.
cuttingSafety.escapeRoute: Always have a clear escape route.
cuttingSafety.chainSharpness: Sharp chains reduce kickback and improve control.

stormSafety.unstableWood: Storm-damaged wood is unpredictable. Use extra caution.
stormSafety.rootLift: Uprooted trees can roll or collapse.

jobsiteSafety.setup: Stage gear, set boundaries, and identify hazards.
jobsiteSafety.crewRoles: Assign climber, ground sawyer, rope handler, and spotter.
jobsiteSafety.trafficControl: Use cones, tape, and signs to block off work area.
jobsiteSafety.customerSafety: Keep customers away from drop zone.

emergencyProtocol.call911: If someone is hurt, bleeding, unconscious, or in danger, call 911 immediately.
emergencyProtocol.fallResponse: Do not move victim unless necessary.
emergencyProtocol.chainsawInjury: Stop bleeding, call emergency services, and stabilize.

weatherSafety.rain: Wet bark reduces grip and increases slip risk.
weatherSafety.cold: Cold stiffens ropes and reduces flexibility.

riskManagement.hazardAssessment: Identify dead limbs, cracks, rot, and weak attachments.
riskManagement.treeInspection: Check bark, roots, canopy, and trunk.
riskManagement.toolPlacement: Keep tools organized and away from ropes.
